meta.description: Texas beta outreach targets for BioMate

targets.name: UT Southwestern — Lyda Hill Department of Bioinformatics
targets.notes: Premier regional bioinformatics hub. BioHPC world-class computing infrastructure. 8 active faculty with broad multi-omics scope. Strong translational push makes QC governance a key selling point.

targets.name: Baylor College of Medicine — Human Genome Sequencing Center (HGSC)
targets.reach_channel: cold-email, Texas Medical Center networking, conference (ASHG)
targets.notes: 180+ staff, 36,000 sq ft. Founding Human Genome Project member. Enormous throughput — QC governance and batch-run automation are directly relevant to their scale.

targets.name: UTHealth Houston — McWilliams School of Biomedical Informatics
targets.notes: Only advanced doctoral biomedical informatics program in Texas. 130+ faculty, 400+ graduate students. Strong AI + data science track — BioMate could be embedded in curriculum.

targets.name: MD Anderson Cancer Center — Bioinformatics & Computational Biology
targets.notes: Top-ranked cancer center globally. Heavy multi-omics pipeline usage. QC governance for clinical translation is a key fit. TCGA-scale reproducibility matters here.

targets.name: Rice University — Treangen Lab (Metagenomics & Computational Biology)
targets.notes: NSF/NIH/CDC funded. AI2Health initiative. Graph-based genomic variation tools. Direct overlap with BioMate metagenomics + QC workflows. Also relevant to energy-sector bioremediation angle.

targets.name: Baylor College of Medicine — Quantitative & Computational Biosciences (QCB) Program
targets.notes: Multi-institutional consortium (BCM + Rice + UH + MD Anderson). Strong translational drug discovery angle. BioMate curriculum integration opportunity.

targets.name: UT Austin — Center for Computational Biology and Bioinformatics (CCBB)
targets.notes: Deep learning for macromolecular structure prediction + genome-scale drug design. Protein/cryo-EM workflows directly relevant.

targets.name: UT Austin — UTEX Culture Collection of Algae
targets.notes: World's largest algae culture collection. Genomics + genetic engineering for biofuels, CO2 mitigation, pharmaceuticals. Prime energy-biology target.

targets.name: Texas A&M University — Institute for Genome Sciences and Society (TIGSS)
targets.notes: TIGSS bioinformatics core (2012+). TxGen agricultural genomics service. Dr. Joshua Yuan holds world record algae productivity (43.3 g/m²/day outdoor trial). Energy-biology overlap is very strong.

targets.name: Texas A&M AgriLife Genomics & Bioinformatics Service (TxGen)
targets.notes: State-run genomics service. High throughput. QC governance + reproducibility angle maps well to service core model.

targets.name: UTMB Galveston — Bioinformatics & Genomics Lab (BGL)
targets.reach_channel: cold-email, DHS/DTRA contacts, environmental genomics conferences
targets.notes: $10M+ funding from DHS, DTRA, NIH. Novel pathogen detection, complex environmental microbiome analysis. Industrial biotech / energy-sector bioremediation crossover possible.

targets.name: Texas A&M University Galveston — Microalgae Research Lab
targets.notes: Focus on microalgae growth conditions and long-chain hydrocarbon biosynthesis for biofuels. ExxonMobil has historically partnered with similar algae programs.

targets.name: UT Dallas — Genome Center & Bioinformatics Program
targets.notes: 10x Genomics Chromium X + NextSeq 2000 installed. MS bioinformatics program trains pipeline-hungry students. Michael Zhang is a very well-known PI (SEQLOGO, cis-regulatory element work).

targets.name: Rice University — AI2Health Initiative & Computational Biology Group
targets.notes: AI2Health spans systems biology, structural biology, metagenomics. Protein/cryo-EM workflows directly relevant.

targets.name: University of Houston — Computational Biology & Bioinformatics
targets.notes: Part of the BCM/Rice/UH multi-institutional consortium. Growing research infrastructure.

targets.name: UTSA — Wang Lab (Bioinformatics & Microbial Genomics)
targets.notes: Computational approaches to microbial data. Graduate-level bioinformatics course (CS5263). Smaller lab — good early adopter candidate.

targets.name: UT Health San Antonio — Genomics & Precision Medicine
targets.notes: Growing precision medicine infrastructure. Clinical QC governance angle.

targets.name: Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center — Genomics Program
targets.notes: West Texas hub. Growing bioinformatics infrastructure. Pharmacogenomics angle relevant to drug discovery paper.

targets.name: St. Mary's University — MS in Medical Genomics (launching Fall 2026)
targets.notes: New program launching Fall 2026 — excellent BioMate curriculum integration opportunity at the founding stage.

targets.name: Texas Medical Center (TMC) — Institutional Umbrella
targets.reach_channel: TMC Innovation Hub, institutional-partnership, TMC3 collaborative
targets.notes: Largest medical complex in the world. 60+ institutions, 106,000+ employees. TMC3 is a $1.5B research complex. BioMate institutional licensing is the play here.

targets.name: UT Southwestern — Simmons Comprehensive Cancer Center
targets.reach_channel: cold-email, AACR conference, clinical genomics networks
targets.notes: NCI-designated comprehensive cancer center. Translational genomics pipeline — QC governance is directly relevant to clinical trial data integrity.

targets.name: Houston Methodist Research Institute
targets.notes: Part of TMC. Strong translational and proteomics program.

targets.name: Texas Children's Hospital — Jan and Dan Duncan Neurological Research Institute
targets.reach_channel: TMC networking, cold-email, rare disease conferences
targets.notes: BCM/Texas Children's joint institute. Pediatric rare disease + neurogenomics. Variant calling + clinical QC angle.

targets.name: Baylor Scott & White Health — Genomics & Precision Medicine
targets.notes: Largest not-for-profit healthcare system in Texas. Clinical genomics operations at scale.

targets.name: Children's Medical Center Dallas — Genomics & Rare Disease
targets.notes: UT Southwestern-affiliated children's hospital. Rare disease genomics at scale.

targets.name: Baylor Genetics — Clinical Genomics Testing
targets.reach_channel: cold-email, clinical lab networks, BCM connections
targets.notes: Commercial genomics testing lab spun from BCM. QC governance + audit trail is essential for CLIA/CAP compliance. Excellent fit.

targets.name: NeuroX1 — Generative AI Drug Discovery (Neurological Disorders)
targets.notes: Austin-based AI drug discovery startup. BioMate's ADMET + pharmacogenomics + proteomics workflows directly complement their generative AI target ID pipeline.

targets.name: Colossal Biosciences — CRISPR De-extinction
targets.notes: Mammoth, dodo, thylacine CRISPR projects. Massive WGS + comparative genomics workload. High-profile company, could be strong brand endorser.

targets.name: XBiotech — Natural Human Antibody Therapeutics
targets.notes: Focuses on antibodies derived from natural human immunity. BioMate proteomics + immunophenotyping workflows are directly applicable.

targets.name: Salarius Pharmaceuticals — Epigenetic Oncology
targets.reach_channel: cold-email, Houston biotech network, AACR conference
targets.notes: Epigenetic therapies (LSD1 inhibitors) for rare pediatric cancers. ChIP-seq / ATAC-seq workflows map directly to their MOA studies.

targets.name: ImmunoMet Therapeutics — Metabolism-Targeted Anti-Cancer
targets.notes: Cellular metabolism for anti-cancer/anti-fibrosis. Multi-omics integration workflows relevant.

targets.name: Mirna Therapeutics — microRNA-Based Oncology
targets.notes: microRNA mimics for oncology. Small RNA-seq and functional genomics workflows relevant.

targets.name: Nanoscope Therapeutics — Optogenetic Gene Therapy
targets.notes: Ambient light-sensitive molecules for retinal degeneration. Multi-modal genomics workload.

targets.name: ARPA-H Dallas Hub — Biomedical Innovation Ecosystem
targets.notes: 1 of 3 national ARPA-H hubs. $2.5B federal program. Dallas-based hub represents an entire ecosystem of funded startups and academic partners — strategic umbrella partnership opportunity.

targets.name: GenPrex — Lung Cancer Gene Therapy
targets.notes: TUSC2 gene therapy for lung cancer. Basic genomics workload.

targets.name: Gameto — Female Reproductive Biotech
targets.notes: Ovarian aging + fertility. Single-cell genomics workflows relevant.

targets.name: GENAC — Genomic & Experimental Neurobiology & Aging Center
targets.notes: Genomics + neurobiology + aging convergence. Drug discovery pipeline angle.

targets.name: Texas Pharmacogenomics Consulting
targets.notes: Niche pharmacogenomics consultancy. BioMate pharmacogenomics workflows (CYP2D6, TPMT, DPYD) are a direct fit.

targets.name: Igenbio — Genomics for Bioremediation
targets.reach_channel: cold-email, energy-biotech conferences, Houston industry networks
targets.notes: Company explicitly offering genome sequencing + analysis for bioremediation acceleration. BioMate metagenomics QC + functional annotation workflows are a direct product fit. Potential OEM/partnership play.

targets.name: Texas Biotechnology Inc. — Recombinant Enzyme Design
targets.notes: Genetic manipulation for degradation of salts, pesticides, petrochemical pollutants. Proteomics + functional annotation workflows relevant.

targets.name: Advanced Microbial Solutions — Petroleum Site Bioremediation
targets.notes: Active in TX, OK, KS, AR, MO. Microbial remediation of petroleum-contaminated sites. Metagenomics characterization of site microbiomes.

targets.name: Drylet — Industrial Wastewater Bioremediation
targets.notes: Venture-backed; industrial + municipal wastewater bioremediation. Microbiome characterization workflows.

targets.name: ExxonMobil — Advanced Biofuels Research Division
targets.notes: $600M algae biofuels program (Synthetic Genomics partnership). Paused algae commercialization 2023 but research continues. Multi-omics strain optimization workflows directly relevant.

targets.name: Texas A&M — Reservoir Microbiome & MEOR Research
targets.reach_channel: cold-email, SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) networking
targets.notes: MEOR research using 16S rRNA metagenomics to characterize halophilic microbes in petroleum reservoirs. Direct BioMate metagenomics workflow fit.

targets.name: ETEC Inc. — Advanced Bioremediation Services
targets.notes: Environmental remediation services. Potential metagenomics characterization customer.

targets.name: Texas Biomedical Research Institute (TBRI)
targets.notes: Largest standalone biomedical research institute in Texas (~$100M+ annual budget). Former Southwest Foundation for Biomedical Research. Specializes in infectious disease, virology, and comparative genomics using non-human primate models. Major NIH-funded sequencing infrastructure. Key omission from original list.

targets.name: Dell Medical School — UT Austin (Precision Medicine & Genomics)
targets.reach_channel: cold-email, Austin biotech network, UT Austin institutional contacts
targets.notes: UT Austin's medical school, opened 2016 and growing rapidly. Strong precision medicine and clinical genomics program. Located in the heart of the Austin biotech corridor alongside Dell Seton Medical Center. Growing bioinformatics infrastructure — QC governance for clinical trial genomics is a direct fit.

targets.name: University of North Texas Health Science Center (UNTHSC)
targets.reach_channel: cold-email, forensic genetics conferences (ISFG, AAFS), pharmacogenomics networks
targets.notes: Nationally recognized forensic genetics program (DNA identity laboratory). Also runs pharmacogenomics and health disparities genomics research. Covers Fort Worth — an underrepresented node in the current target list (only Dallas was covered for north Texas). Bruce Budowle is a world authority in forensic genomics.

targets.name: University of Texas Rio Grande Valley — Biomedical Sciences & Genomics
targets.reach_channel: cold-email, NIH RCMI program contacts, health disparities conferences
targets.notes: Growing genomics program in the Rio Grande Valley. Focus on Hispanic/Latino population health disparities — an underserved genomics niche. NIH RCMI-funded institution. Geographic gap filler for South Texas.

targets.name: Baylor University — Biochemistry & Molecular Biology
targets.notes: Research university in Waco. Smaller bioinformatics footprint than major Texas institutions but represents the Central Texas corridor between Austin and Dallas. Potential for early adopter individual labs.

targets.name: Texas Southern University — Biology & Health Sciences (HBCU)
targets.reach_channel: cold-email, NIH BUILD / RCMI HBCU programs
targets.notes: HBCU in Houston with growing biomedical research. NIH RCMI and BUILD programs fund genomics infrastructure at HBCUs. Important for equity-focused outreach and federal grant alignment. Limited bioinformatics infrastructure currently but trajectory is positive.

targets.name: MD Anderson Cancer Center — Proteomics & Metabolomics Core Facility
targets.reach_channel: cold-email, ASMS conference (American Society for Mass Spectrometry), internal MD Anderson contacts
targets.notes: Distinct from the Bioinformatics & Computational Biology department (Ken Chen). The proteomics core is a separate service unit running MaxQuant and DIA-NN analyses for dozens of internal MD Anderson labs. BioMate's LC-MS/MS proteomics workflows with QC governance are a direct service-core fit. Separate outreach from the bioinformatics dept entry.

targets.name: Memorial Hermann Health System — Clinical Genomics
targets.reach_channel: TMC networking, cold-email, clinical lab associations
targets.notes: One of the largest not-for-profit health systems in Houston (17 hospitals, 6,000+ physicians). Part of the Texas Medical Center but independent procurement from the TMC umbrella. Running clinical genomics for cancer and rare disease at substantial scale. CLIA/CAP compliance requirements make BioMate's audit trail a direct fit.

targets.name: Texas Heart Institute — Cardiovascular Genomics
targets.reach_channel: TMC networking, cold-email, AHA/ACC conference (cardiovascular genomics sessions)
targets.notes: Standalone research institute at the Texas Medical Center, not covered under the TMC umbrella entry (independent procurement). Runs RNA-seq and single-cell genomics for cardiac regeneration and heart failure research. Strong translational push — QC governance for clinical translation is a direct need.

targets.name: Cook Children's Health Care System — Genomics & Rare Disease
targets.reach_channel: cold-email, pediatric genomics networks, ACMG conference
targets.notes: Independent pediatric health system in Fort Worth (not affiliated with Children's Medical Center Dallas). Rare disease genomics and pharmacogenomics program. Completes the north Texas pediatric genomics picture alongside CMC Dallas.

targets.name: AstraZeneca — BioHub at TMC3 (Houston)
targets.reach_channel: TMC3 partnership process, AstraZeneca innovation contacts, LinkedIn
targets.notes: AstraZeneca opened a BioHub at the TMC3 campus as part of their global network of open innovation hubs. They co-invest in early-stage biotech and run internal multi-omics R&D. An enterprise partnership here would have global reach given AstraZeneca's international BioHub network. Primary focus: oncology and cardiovascular.

targets.name: Thermo Fisher Scientific — R&D Operations (Austin)
targets.notes: Thermo Fisher has significant R&D operations in Austin (legacy Life Technologies / Ion Torrent). They develop sequencing reagents and run internal genomics QC pipelines. Long-term partnership angle: BioMate as an analysis layer on top of their sequencing platforms. Decision cycle is long (large corporation) — watch list for partnership opportunity.

targets.name: Sonic Healthcare USA — Clinical Genomics & Pathology
targets.reach_channel: cold-email, Austin biotech network, CAP/CLIA lab conferences (AACC, CAP)
targets.notes: US headquarters is Austin, TX. One of the top-5 clinical diagnostics companies in the US (~$3B revenue). Operates clinical genomics labs (including CPL — Clinical Pathology Laboratories) across the country. CLIA/CAP certified. Runs NGS-based oncology panels, hereditary cancer testing, and pharmacogenomics. BioMate's evidence-graded QC audit trails are a direct compliance fit for their regulatory obligations. Highest-priority diagnostic lab target because of Austin HQ.

targets.name: Quest Diagnostics — Advanced Diagnostics & Genomics (Texas)
targets.reach_channel: cold-email, AACC / CAP conference, clinical genomics networks
targets.notes: Largest clinical laboratory company in the US. Major Texas operations (Dallas regional hub). Runs extensive NGS-based testing: FoundationOne-equivalent oncology panels, hereditary cancer (BRCA, Lynch), pharmacogenomics (CYP2D6, TPMT, DPYD), carrier screening. QC governance + audit trail is operationally critical for CAP/CLIA compliance. Decision cycle is long (large corporation + procurement) but contract size is enterprise. Note: Quest is already on the national CRO list — this entry covers Texas-specific outreach to regional lab directors.

targets.name: Labcorp Diagnostics — Genomics & Molecular Pathology (Texas)
targets.reach_channel: cold-email, CAP / AACC conference, clinical genomics networks
targets.notes: IMPORTANT DISTINCTION: This entry targets Labcorp's clinical diagnostics division (CLIA/CAP certified patient testing). The CRO segment already includes 'Labcorp Drug Development (Covance)' — that is the pharma contract research arm and is a completely separate business unit with different buyers. This entry is for the clinical lab side: hereditary cancer panels, pharmacogenomics, oncology NGS. Large Houston regional presence. Same compliance-driven QC audit trail need as Quest.

targets.name: Myriad Genetics — Hereditary Cancer & Pharmacogenomics Testing (Texas)
targets.reach_channel: cold-email, ASCO / AACR conference, hereditary cancer networks
targets.notes: National genetic testing company (HQ: Salt Lake City) with a very large Texas customer base — MD Anderson, UTSouthwestern, and Texas oncology practices are major referrers. Runs myRisk (hereditary cancer), GeneSight (pharmacogenomics for psychiatry), and tumor profiling panels. Serves Texas extensively through molecular pathology networks. QC governance for hereditary cancer panel variant interpretation is a direct fit. National HQ but included here because of outsized Texas clinical presence.

targets.name: GeneDx — Pediatric & Rare Disease Genetic Testing (Texas)
targets.reach_channel: cold-email, ACMG conference, pediatric genetics networks, Texas Children's / Cook Children's connections
targets.notes: Leading national genetic testing lab for pediatric and rare disease (formerly BioReference Genomics division). Major referral volumes from Texas Children's Hospital, Cook Children's, and Children's Medical Center Dallas. Clinical WGS and WES for undiagnosed rare disease is their primary workload — BioMate's variant calling QC governance and audit trails are directly applicable. National HQ but serving Texas pediatric centers at scale.

targets.name: CHRISTUS Health — Laboratory & Genomics Services
targets.reach_channel: cold-email, Catholic health system networks, Texas clinical lab associations
targets.notes: Large Catholic health system headquartered in Irving, TX (Dallas area). Operates hospitals and clinics across Texas, Louisiana, New Mexico, and internationally (Mexico, Chile, Colombia). Running clinical genomics and pharmacogenomics programs at scale. CLIA/CAP certified lab network. QC governance + audit trails for compliance is a strong pitch. Texas HQ makes this a higher-priority target than national chains.
